```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```


#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Load libraries and dataset

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)   
tidymodels_prefer()
library(rpart)   # for modeling decision trees
library(rpart.plot)   # for plotting decision trees
library(vip)          

ames <- read_csv("AmesHousing.csv")   # load dataset

# convert all character variables to factor variables
ames <- ames |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Data exploration

```{r}
library(skimr)

skim(ames)

# mix of numerical and categorical (ordinal and nominal) features
# 113 missing entries in 'Gr_Liv_Area'
# feature 'Overall_Qual' is ordinal, levels need to be reordered
# numerical features have different SDs

```


```{r}
# reorder levels of 'Overall_Qual' (default order is alphabetical)

ames <- ames |>
  mutate(Overall_Qual = factor(Overall_Qual,
                               levels = c("Very_Poor", "Poor", "Fair", "Below_Average",
                                          "Average", "Above_Average", "Good", "Very_Good",
                                          "Excellent", "Very_Excellent")))

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Data splitting

```{r}
# data splitting

set.seed(208)

ames_split <- initial_split(data = ames, prop = 0.8)

ames_train <- training(ames_split)   # training set
ames_test <- testing(ames_split)     # test set

```


```{r}
library(caret)

nearZeroVar(ames_train, saveMetrics = TRUE)

# five nzv features - 'Street', 'Utilities', 'Pool_Area', 'Screen_Porch', 'Misc_Val'

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Recipe and blueprint

```{r}
# create the feature engineering blueprint

ames_blueprint <- recipe(Sale_Price ~ ., data = ames_train) |>
  step_nzv(Street, Utilities, Pool_Area, Screen_Porch, Misc_Val) |>   # remove nzv features
  step_impute_mean(Gr_Liv_Area) |>                                    # impute missing entries
  step_integer(Overall_Qual) |>                                       # label encoding
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>                         # center and scale
  step_other(Neighborhood, threshold = 0.01, other = "other") |>      # lump rare neighborhoods
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = FALSE)               # dummy encode

```


```{r}
# blueprint check
# summary of engineered training set

ames_blueprint |> 
  prep() |> 
  bake(new_data = NULL) |> 
  skimr::skim()

```


```{r}
# blueprint check
# summary of engineered test set

ames_blueprint |> 
  prep() |> 
  bake(new_data = ames_test) |> 
  skimr::skim()

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Model specification and workflow

```{r}
# model specification: cost_complexity (rpart's cp) to be tuned
# tree_depth and min_n are set to rpart's own defaults 
# they are hyperparameters too, and could be tuned

tree_spec <- decision_tree(cost_complexity = tune(),
                           tree_depth = 30,   # rpart's maxdepth
                           min_n = 20) |>     # rpart's minsplit
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")   # use "classification" for classification tasks


# workflow
tree_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(ames_blueprint) |>
  add_model(tree_spec)

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Cross-validation

```{r}
# CV specifications: 10 folds, 1 repeat

set.seed(208)

ames_folds <- vfold_cv(ames_train, 
                       v = 10,
                       repeats = 1)

```


```{r}
# grid of 20 cost_complexity values, evenly spaced on the log10 scale
# create a smaller grid if computationally expensive

cp_grid <- grid_regular(cost_complexity(), levels = 20)
# cp_min_n_grid <- grid_regular(cost_complexity(), min_n(), levels = 5)

cp_grid

```


```{r}
# implement CV to tune cost_complexity

set.seed(208)

tree_cv <- tune_grid(tree_wf,
                     resamples = ames_folds,
                     grid = cp_grid,
                     metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq))   # use appropriate metrics for classification tasks

```


```{r}
# CV results

collect_metrics(tree_cv)

```


```{r}
# plotting CV results (x-axis is on the log10 scale)

autoplot(tree_cv)

```


```{r}
# top 5 cp values by RMSE

show_best(tree_cv, metric = "rmse")  # use appropriate metrics for classification tasks

```


```{r}
# optimal hyperparameter
# use appropriate metrics for classification tasks

best_cp <- select_best(tree_cv, metric = "rmse")
best_cp

best_cp_1se <- select_by_one_std_err(tree_cv, desc(cost_complexity), metric = "rmse")
best_cp_1se

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Final model and test set evaluation

```{r}
# build optimal final model

# plug best cp into the workflow
final_tree_wf <- finalize_workflow(tree_wf, best_cp_1se)  # or use best_cp

# fit on the full training set and evaluate once on the test set
final_tree_fit <- last_fit(final_tree_wf,
                           split = ames_split,
                           metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq)) # use appropriate metrics for classification tasks

# test set RMSE and R-squared
collect_metrics(final_tree_fit)  

```


```{r}
#| eval: false

# for general classification tasks and predictions on test set

test_preds <- collect_predictions(final_tree_fit)

# plug in the response variable name
test_preds |>
  select(<response>, .pred_class, .pred_Yes, .pred_No) |>
  head()

# confusion matrix
test_preds |>
  conf_mat(truth = <response>, estimate = .pred_class)

# confusion matrix summary
test_preds |>
  conf_mat(truth = <response>, estimate = .pred_class) |> 
  summary()

# ROC curve (use the probability of the FIRST level, "Yes")
test_preds |>
  roc_curve(truth = <response>, .pred_Yes) |>
  autoplot()

# ROC AUC
test_preds |>
  roc_auc(truth = <response>, .pred_Yes)

```


```{r}
#| eval: false

# for project (since hotel_bookings_test doesn't include response)

final_tree_wf <- finalize_workflow(tree_wf, best_cp)

final_tree_fit <- fit(final_tree_wf, data = hotel_bookings_train)

test_preds <- augment(final_tree_fit, new_data = hotel_bookings_test)

# .pred_Yes = P(response = Yes), use this for Kaggle submission
test_preds |>
  select(id, .pred_class, .pred_Yes, .pred_No) |>
  head()

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Tree summary and variable importance

```{r}
# pull out the underlying rpart object for rpart-specific tools
tree_engine <- extract_fit_engine(final_tree_fit)

# number of terminal nodes (leaves)
sum(tree_engine$frame$var == "<leaf>")

```


```{r}
# detailed model summary (long output!)

summary(tree_engine)

```


```{r}
# visualize tree

rpart.plot(tree_engine, roundint = FALSE)

```


```{r}
# variable importance

tree_vi <- vip::vi(tree_engine) |> 
  mutate(Importance_pct = round(100 * Importance / sum(Importance), 1))

# variable importance plot
tree_vi |>
  slice_max(Importance_pct, n = 15) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Importance_pct, y = fct_reorder(Variable, Importance_pct))) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) str_trunc(x, 30)) +
  labs(y = NULL)

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Regression tree (no pruning): Ames Housing dataset

```{r}
# same workflow, new model spec: cost_complexity = 0 means no pruning

# model specification
tree_noprune_spec <- decision_tree(cost_complexity = 0,
                                   tree_depth = 30,
                                   min_n = 20) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")   # use "classification" for classification tasks


# workflow
tree_noprune_wf <- tree_wf |>
  update_model(tree_noprune_spec)

```


```{r}
# fit on training set, evaluate on test set

noprune_fit <- last_fit(tree_noprune_wf,
                        split = ames_split,
                        metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq))

# test set RMSE
collect_metrics(noprune_fit)

```


```{r}
# number of leaves: pruned vs. unpruned

sum(extract_fit_engine(noprune_fit)$frame$var == "<leaf>")

```


```{r}
# visualize tree

rpart.plot(extract_fit_engine(noprune_fit), roundint = FALSE)

```



#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Regression tree (minimal feature engineering): Ames Housing dataset

```{r}
# new blueprint: only impute the missing entries

ames_blueprint_min <- recipe(Sale_Price ~ ., data = ames_train) |>
  step_impute_mean(Gr_Liv_Area)


# same workflow, new recipe
tree_min_wf <- tree_wf |>
  update_recipe(ames_blueprint_min)

```


```{r}
# implement CV to tune cost_complexity
# same folds and same grid as before, so the comparison is fair

tree_cv_min <- tune_grid(tree_min_wf,
                         resamples = ames_folds,
                         grid = cp_grid,
                         metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq))

```


```{r}
# CV results

collect_metrics(tree_cv_min)

```


```{r}
# optimal hyperparameter
# use appropriate metrics for classification tasks

best_cp_min <- select_best(tree_cv_min, metric = "rmse")
best_cp_min

best_cp_1se_min <- select_by_one_std_err(tree_cv_min, desc(cost_complexity), metric = "rmse")
best_cp_1se_min

```


```{r}
# DEMONSTRATION
# compare the best CV RMSE: full feature engineering vs. minimal

bind_rows(
  full_fe = show_best(tree_cv, metric = "rmse", n = 1),
  minimal_fe = show_best(tree_cv_min, metric = "rmse", n = 1),
  .id = "recipe"
) |>
  select(recipe, cost_complexity, mean, std_err)

```
